skill.name: fix-my-ending
skill.description: Diagnose why a post's ending is not earning a reply, then rewrite it or remove it. Use when someone asks for a call to action, says nobody comments, asks how to end a post, or has closed with a question that reads as asking a favour. Do not bolt an engagement prompt onto a post that was already finished, and do not promise that a new ending will bring comments.
skill.summary: Diagnose, rewrite, or remove post endings based on the purpose of the post.
skill.author: prateeks367

Optional VoiceMOAT integration is described, but its implementation and data handling are outside this file.

content.value_statement: Generic closing questions can weaken posts and ask readers for unnecessary effort. This skill diagnoses the ending and rewrites or removes it to match the purpose.
actual_capabilities: Identify whether a post aims to inform, invite disagreement, encourage saving, start a conversation, or invite private messages.
Classify endings as favor requests, summaries, lessons, pitches, genuine questions, or no separate ending.
Test whether a stranger can answer a closing question in one sentence without research, rereading, or prior agreement.
Rewrite endings around specific experiences, expected disagreements, concrete examples, or the strongest existing line.
Recommend deleting explanations that weaken the final moment of a story.
When VoiceMOAT is connected, use documented tools for platform-specific voice profiles, voice matching, and whole-post improvement.
limitations: Cannot guarantee comments, replies, visibility, or engagement.
Does not write transactional engagement prompts such as requests to comment a keyword for a template.
VoiceMOAT features require a connected service and a Pro or Enterprise plan.
The skill file documents VoiceMOAT tools but does not include their implementation or data handling details.

use_cases.title: Revise a professional post
use_cases.description: Replace a generic closing question with a specific question that matches the intended conversation.

use_cases.title: Preserve a story ending
use_cases.description: Remove an unnecessary explanation after the final story moment without adding a call to action.

use_cases.title: Review client closing lines
use_cases.description: Check whether a closing pitch fits the post and whether the ending preserves the client voice.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an ending
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this post: [post]. Identify its purpose and ending type. Explain whether the last line supports that purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a closing question
prompt_templates.prompt: This post should start a conversation: [post]. Test its closing question and rewrite it so a stranger can answer from personal experience.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate revision of a conversation post

prompt_templates.title: Choose what to remove
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this story post: [post]. Decide whether the final explanation or question should be deleted. Provide the revised ending and your reasoning.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced editing of a story conclusion

prompt_templates.title: Check purpose and platform voice
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [LinkedIn or Twitter] post: [post]. Diagnose its purpose and ending. With VoiceMOAT connected, check voice consistency and revise the whole post only if needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with optional VoiceMOAT integration

output_examples.input: A post explains how long approval chains delay releases. It ends with: Thoughts?
output: Purpose: Start a conversation about approval delays.
Diagnosis: The closing question requests broad feedback without a specific focus.
Revised ending: Which approval step most often delays your releases?

output_examples.input: A story ends with: She closed the laptop and went home on time. Then it adds: This proves that boundaries matter.
output: Purpose: Help the reader understand the story.
Diagnosis: The final explanation repeats what the story already communicates.
Recommendation: Delete the explanation and end with: She closed the laptop and went home on time.

output_examples.input: A reusable onboarding checklist ends with: Agree?
output: Purpose: Give readers a checklist they can save and reuse.
Diagnosis: The question asks for agreement that the checklist does not need.
Recommendation: Remove the question and end on the final checklist item.

best_practices: Provide the full post and its intended purpose before requesting an ending revision.
Use closing questions that readers can answer from their own experience in one sentence.
Accept deletion when the final story moment already completes the post.
anti_patterns: Add a generic request for comments to every post regardless of its purpose.
Expect a revised ending to guarantee replies or compensate for limited reach.
Copy another writer's closing style or use transactional engagement prompts.

faq.question: What does this skill change?
faq.answer: It diagnoses the purpose and ending of a post, then recommends rewriting, moving the strongest line, or deleting the ending.

faq.question: Does every post need a closing question?
faq.answer: No. Informative posts, reusable material, and stories can end without asking readers to reply.

faq.question: Will it guarantee more comments?
faq.answer: No. Replies also depend on the audience, visibility, surrounding content, and whether readers have something to contribute.

faq.question: Can it write engagement prompts that offer rewards for comments?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly rejects transactional prompts such as asking readers to comment a keyword for a template.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT for basic editing?
faq.answer: No. The core review uses the supplied draft. Optional VoiceMOAT features require a connection and a Pro or Enterprise plan.

faq.question: What does the optional VoiceMOAT connection add?
faq.answer: It provides separate LinkedIn and Twitter voice profiles, voice matching checks, and whole-post improvement when the purpose needs clarification.
